title: The same write delivered twice at the same time

R1.reason: Idempotency-Key per tap reused on retry, PK scoped by tenant, user, operation and key, sha256 fingerprint, stored in PostgreSQL.

R2.reason: Key row, business writes and response update share one transaction. The concurrent duplicate waits on the unique index and then replays, or returns 409 IN_PROGRESS with Retry-After after lock_timeout.

R3.reason: Same key with a different fingerprint returns 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. A test covers it.

R4.reason: UNIQUE(voucher_id) on voucher_redemptions, an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE redeemed_at IS NULL, and a ledger UNIQUE(reason, source_id). It explains the change to (voucher_id, user_id) for once-per-user.

R5.reason: Concurrent Promise.all tests on real PostgreSQL, both same-key and different-key, plus rollback and lock_timeout tests.

forbidden.item: In-memory deduplication or a Redis TTL key as the only guard
forbidden.evidence: It explicitly rejects an in-memory Set and Redis SETNX, and uses PostgreSQL.

forbidden.item: Check then insert without a unique constraint
forbidden.evidence: It uses an atomic UPDATE with a WHERE condition, unique constraints and INSERT ON CONFLICT.

forbidden.item: Relying on a queue job id for uniqueness
forbidden.evidence: It explicitly rejects a queue jobId.

forbidden.item: Telling the client to generate a new key on retry
forbidden.evidence: The client sends the same UUID on every retry. A new key is generated only for a new tap after a definite failure.

grade.summary: A thorough answer that covers all five rubric items and violates no forbidden decision.
